title: Introduce stream-proxy: preflight cred-priming, heartbeat publishers, and tri-SDK version bumps
author: Ava Chen
description: Problem: multiple SDKs independently were doing cred pre-warm, heartbeat, and streamed telemetry which caused duplicated requests, token churn, and mismatched heartbeat intervals across languages. This led to spiky auth calls under bursty workloads and noisy telemetry. Goal: provide a single lightweight in-repo "stream-proxy" primitive that centralizes preflight credential priming, lightweight heartbeat publishers for long-lived streams, and a compact telemetry envelope for streamed metrics. The change harmonizes behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, reduces auth thundering, and enables a safer default for session lifetime handling. Summary of changes: - Add a small in-repo stream-proxy component (lib/stream_proxy/) that exposes an opinionated REST-compatible boundary used by SDK adapters. The proxy supports: cred-priming (pre-warm token and short-lived lease), heartbeat publisher (periodic keepalive events with exponential backoff on failure), and streamed_metrics envelope (compact binary/JSON variant selectable by SDK). - SDK adapters: python/ts/go subpackages updated to call the proxy during session open, to subscribe/unsubscribe heartbeat publishers when streams start/stop, and to emit streamed_metrics via the proxy rather than directly to the telemetry backend. - Ergonomics: simplified client API surface for streaming to a single method on the sdk client: start_stream(options) with opt-in advanced hooks for custom heartbeat intervals and preflight scope. This reduces ceremony for the common case. - Backwards compatibility: when the proxy is not available (older deployments), SDKs fall back to previous per-language behavior; we added a detection and a conservative retry/jitter profile so behavior remains stable. - Version bumps: synchronized minor bumps for SDK packages to make the new ergonomics available: python 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5, typescript 1.6.0 -> 1.6.1, go 1.8.2 -> 1.8.3; changelogs included. Migration notes: - Existing consumers need not change immediately. To opt in to the proxy behavior, set client.start_stream({enable_proxy: true}) or set REDWOOD_STREAM_PROXY=1 in environment. - If you manage a Private deployment, see deployments/stream_proxy/README.md for install/compat notes; the proxy is optional but recommended for high-throughput stream workloads. Testing and verification: unit tests for proxy logic, adapter integration tests for Py/TS/Go, and a lightweight throughput canary in perf-canary/stream-proxy-test. We ran canary traffic for 72h across regions (us-west1/eu-west1) with telemetry validated and auth calls reduced by ~65% under synthetic bursts. Rollout: staged rollout on hosted API with feature-flag gate; automatic fallback on proxy error conditions. Why this is different: rather than adding per-SDK heuristics we provide a thin, deployable coordinator that keeps language ergonomics simple while centralizing auth/heartbeat behavior.

release_notes: - Added optional in-repo stream-proxy to centralize credential priming and heartbeat publishing across SDKs; opt-in via enable_proxy or env var. - SDKs (Python/TS/Go) updated with lightweight stream adapter and simplified start_stream API. - Reduced auth churn and duplicated telemetry under bursty workloads. - Minor SDK version bumps: py->0.12.5, ts->1.6.1, go->1.8.3.
notes: This PR coordinates code across SDKs and the deployable proxy. Operations should coordinate a staged rollout if you host the private control plane. If deploying the proxy in private clusters, ensure KMS keys are configured for the token-lease path.
